brief.headline: Move from immediate payment to 30-day credit to free ₹44.91 L working capital — they already stretch suppliers to 63d vs 6d peer median.

priceAsk.summary: Benchmark laminate price against BOPET film import unit value and press for any gap above 171.60 ₹/kg to be justified or closed.
priceAsk.basis: BOPET film import unit value from UN Comtrade (public preview) sets the market line at 171.60 ₹/kg; any premium over substrate cost must be defensible on conversion value-add.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Shift from Immediate payment to standard 30-day credit; if they resist, settle for 15 additional days as a minimum.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹44.91 L freed at 30-day terms; ₹22.45 L at 15-day terms

brief.financialLeverage: Tetrapak India earns a 5.4% net margin, less than half the 10.2% peer median, so deep price cuts will hurt them. However, they stretch their own payables to 63d vs 6d peer median and run a 75d cash-conversion cycle vs 30d median, proving they value and manage credit aggressively. Their balance sheet carries 1.09x debt-to-equity but interest coverage is comfortable at 10.11x. We represent only 0.12% of their ₹4491.70 Cr revenue (₹5.46 Cr spend), so our standalone leverage is minimal — bundle payment terms, volume commitment, or credible alternate competition to move the needle. A health score of C (59/100) and severe legal case(s) flag continuity risk; secure dual-sourcing and monitor closely.

evidence.point: Their net margin is less than half the peer median, limiting room for price cuts
They already stretch their own suppliers far beyond peer norms
Their cash is tied up much longer than industry standard
We pay them immediately while the market standard is credit
evidence.figure: Current terms: Immediate; working capital freed if 30-day: ₹44.91 L

evidence.point: We are a tiny fraction of their business, so standalone leverage is weak
evidence.figure: ₹5.46 Cr spend is 0.12% of their ₹4491.70 Cr revenue

evidence.point: One in five goods receipts from them gets reversed, signalling quality or paperwork issues

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC — proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets with B health score.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant handling both film substrate and conversion — can second-source at scale with integrated supply chain (C health).

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter specialising in pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong GEEP second-source credentials.

risks: At 0.12% of their revenue, we lack standalone leverage — they can afford to walk unless we bundle volume, multi-year commitment, or credible competition.
Their 5.4% margin vs 10.2% peer median means aggressive price cuts may trigger pushback or force them to cut corners — focus the fight on payment terms where they have room.
Health score C (59/100) and severe legal case(s) raise continuity risk — secure dual-sourcing with Huhtamaki or UFLEX before leaning too hard.
22% goods-receipt reversal rate suggests quality or documentation problems — address root cause now before it escalates into larger commercial disputes.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to align our payment terms with market practice — moving to 30-day credit frees ₹44.91 L for us and mirrors the 63-day payables you already run with your own suppliers.
